ops.text: Those lights on the hill were never marsh-fire; I saw the wings blot out the stars the night I fell.
The old one on the crag only wakes at dusk, so if you mean to go, go now and go gently.
Three ewes gone from the high pasture this month, and not a wolf track among them.
Smoke off the crag again tonight, and my dogs won't face east for any whistle.
The old signpost's eastern arm has been scratched over and newly cut: TO THE CRAG.
The lights on the hill east of the field are the breath of a dragon that sleeps on the crag. The villagers have talked about it for weeks, ever since ewes started going missing from the high pasture.

ops.why: The signpost by the east tree line points to the hills; an old sheep track runs through a gap in the trees at rows 7..8 toward the crag.

ops.title: The Hill Trail
ops.purpose: The climb from the field to the crag, kept by a charcoal-burner who has watched the dragon's fire from his kiln.
ops.sketch: A 2-wide sheep track comes in at the W edge at rows 7..8 from the gap in the field's tree line and climbs east and north-east over rising ground of heather and tall grass, with the mist thinning as it goes. Halfway up, the charcoal-burner Hesketh Wray sits by his smouldering kiln (a campfire) beside a woodpile and a tent. Further up, a scorched patch shows the first signs: blackened rubble, sheep bones, a standing stone with a burn mark. The track leaves by the E edge at rows 7..8 toward the crag. Tree line closes the S, a low cliff closes the N, and the far east beyond the path is denser trees.

ops.title: The Crag
ops.purpose: Where the dragon everyone talks about sleeps, and where the lights on the hill come from.
ops.sketch: The trail comes in at the W edge at rows 7..8 onto a bare, windswept crag top of rock and rubble. In the north-east the ground opens into a scorched hollow ringed by standing stones, and the dragon Orrimund lies coiled there among skull piles, sheep bones and a few dented pieces of old armour, smoke rising from its nostrils. A small shrine near the west end holds offering bowls that the hill folk once left to keep it sleeping. Cliffs close the N, E and S; the only way off is back down the trail.

events.summary: Everyone in Morrows has seen the lights on the eastern hill, so a gap opens in the east tree line, and past it a trail climbs to the crag where the dragon sleeps.

events.text: Those lights on the hill were never marsh-fire; I saw the wings blot out the stars the night I fell.
The old one on the crag only wakes at dusk, so if you mean to go, go now and go gently.
Three ewes gone from the high pasture this month, and not a wolf track among them.
Smoke off the crag again tonight, and my dogs won't face east for any whistle.
The old signpost's eastern arm has been scratched over and newly cut: TO THE CRAG.
